add.waitingForConnectionHelp: This drawer closes when this node is online. You can close it now and check the node list later.
add.commandPlaceholder: Create the node to generate an installation command with its unique Token
add.sshSupportLabel: Does the target machine support SSH?
add.nodeNamePlaceholder: Leave blank to use the hostname on first connection
add.hostAddressHelp: The address the server connects to this host at: an IP, a domain, or the mapped address a platform gives. With a host only, the port is the listen port; when a platform maps the port to another number, give the mapped address and port.
add.targetRequired: Enter an SSH address or ssh command
add.targetHelp: user@host[:port], or paste an ssh command such as ssh -p 2222 root@192.0.2.10
add.installDirHelp: Holds the agent, models and runtime data
add.installDirTooltip: On nodes without docker the runveil runtime keeps images and container root filesystems here too, so choose a local filesystem; a network volume that refuses ':' in file names (such as RunPod's /workspace) does not work.
add.useSystemdTooltip: On: the agent is registered as the gpuworks-agent systemd service, started at boot and restarted when it crashes. Off: the agent runs in the background under nohup, with agent-restart.sh in the install directory for restarting it by hand; the host's existing gpuworks-agent service and agents in other directories are left alone, so another install directory adds one more agent to the same host. Hosts without systemd, or without root or passwordless sudo, always use nohup; macOS nodes use launchd regardless.
add.useSystemdOffHelp: The agent does not start at boot and is not restarted when it exits
add.agentListenAddressHelp: Where the agent listens on this host (or in its container): its --listen.
add.offlineInstructions: The node cannot reach the management node, so it installs from the offline package: download it, copy it to the node (scp, a web terminal or JupyterLab upload), and run the command below in the directory that holds it. The package holds no token and is the same for every node.
add.manualInstructions: First create a node (shown as Connecting until its Agent arrives) to obtain its unique Token, then run the following command on the target machine:
add.tokenSaved: The Token has been minted and saved. You can view or regenerate it from node details.

scheduling.title: Scheduling on {{node}}

blocked.title: This node's runtime cannot use its accelerators
blocked.description:
{{reason}}

Every deployment placed here would fail when its container starts. The platform cordoned the node for this reason and will do so again on its next report unless the cause is fixed.

reason.gpu_plugin_missing: The container runtime {{runtime}} needs the vendor GPU plugin {{plugin}}, which is not installed, so a container cannot be given this node's accelerators.
reason.gpu_runtime_unconfigured: {{runtime}} is running with no GPU support configured, so a container cannot be given this node's accelerators. Installing the vendor plugin is not enough; {{runtime}} has to be told to use it (NVIDIA: nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker, then restart Docker).

help.schedulable: The node takes new replicas. Cordon it to keep new ones off while what runs keeps running, or drain it to also move the replicas placed from a pool onto other nodes.
help.cordoned: No new replica is started here; what runs keeps running. Drain to move the pool-placed replicas off, or make it schedulable again.
help.draining: No new replica is started here. Replacements start on other nodes before existing replicas retire, so service capacity is retained. Pinned replicas wait for a placement change; multi-node and PD units wait until suitable replacement nodes are available.

action.evictConfirm: Take every replica off this node now, without waiting for replacements? Pinned replicas and multi-node or PD ranks wait until the node is schedulable again or their deployment names another node.

done.schedulable: The node takes new replicas again

scheduling.stuck: {{count}} replica(s) are pinned to this node. Change their deployment’s node requirements, or explicitly evict them.

kind.named: Moves its unit after a replacement is ready

scheduling.drainHint: Open Scheduling and drain to see waiting replicas, scheduling feedback, or stop the drain while keeping the node cordoned.
scheduling.waiting: Waiting for {{count}} replica(s) to leave: replacements must be ready before existing service is retired.
scheduling.stopHint: Check each deployment’s latest feedback. You can stop further drain work while keeping the node cordoned; work already in progress may finish. The platform does not automatically enable scheduling or force replicas off the node.
scheduling.completed: No active replicas remain. The node still takes no new replicas; stop the drain to leave it cordoned.
scheduling.retiring: Retiring this instance; waiting for in-flight requests and removal confirmation.
scheduling.pinnedReason: The deployment is pinned to this node. Change its node requirements, or explicitly evict it.
scheduling.lastFailedAttempt: Latest failed attempt on another node: {{message}}
scheduling.awaitingReason: Waiting for a replacement. No scheduling refusal has been reported yet; check the deployment’s instances and model/image preparation.
scheduling.offline: The node is offline: retirement and container removal cannot be confirmed.
scheduling.offlineHint: Restore its agent connection and check its instances. You can stop the drain while keeping the node cordoned; the platform will not enable scheduling or claim that removal succeeded.

disk_low.label: Low disk space
disk_low.impact: Image pulls and model downloads may fail.

runtime_unavailable.label: Container runtime not responding
runtime_unavailable.summary: The selected container runtime query failed.
runtime_unavailable.impact: This node cannot start inference instances.

runtime_provision_failed.label: Runtime setup failed
runtime_provision_failed.summary: The container runtime could not be set up on this node. Its last attempt failed with the error below.
runtime_provision_failed.impact: Every deployment on this node fails until the cause is fixed. The agent tries again by itself, waiting 30 seconds after the first failure and up to 5 minutes later on.

runtime_state_untraversable.label: Runtime user cannot reach the agent directory
runtime_state_untraversable.summary: {{directory}} is not searchable by {{user}}, the user workloads run as, so it cannot reach the agent directory {{stateDir}}.
runtime_state_untraversable.impact: Every workload launch on this node fails with permission denied on the runtime's own files. Open the directory with `{{fix}}`, which grants search only, no listing or writing, or reinstall the agent with an install directory outside it.

path_noexec.label: Path mounted noexec
path_noexec.summary: {{path}} is on {{point}} ({{fstype}}), which is mounted noexec.
path_noexec.impact: Programs the runtime runs from this path cannot start. Install the agent into a directory on a filesystem that allows execution, or remount without noexec.

path_read_only.label: Path mounted read-only
path_read_only.summary: {{path}} is on {{point}} ({{fstype}}), which is mounted read-only.
path_read_only.impact: The agent cannot write models, images or runtime state there. Use a writable directory or remount read-write.

path_ephemeral.label: Data on the container layer
path_ephemeral.summary: {{path}} is on this container's own filesystem layer ({{fstype}} at {{point}}), not on a volume.
path_ephemeral.impact: Models, images and runtime state are lost when the container is recreated. Install the agent into a persistent volume on a local filesystem if the instance has one; a network volume that refuses ':' in file names, such as RunPod's /workspace, cannot hold the runveil runtime's images.

accelerator_probe_failed.label: Accelerator probe failed
accelerator_probe_failed.impact: The accelerators on this node cannot be scheduled.

accelerator_unrecognized.label: Unrecognized accelerator devices
accelerator_unrecognized.summary: This host has PCI devices belonging to a supported vendor that match none of that vendor's rules, usually a model we have not seen.
accelerator_unrecognized.impact: They are left out of the accelerator list and are unavailable for allocation. Send the PCI ids below so the rule can be added.

cuda_init_failed.label: CUDA initialization failed
cuda_init_failed.summary: The CUDA driver failed to initialize. The recheck command prints 0 when initialization succeeds.
cuda_init_failed.impact: This node cannot run CUDA inference.

multi_gpu_check_failed.label: Multi-GPU check failed
multi_gpu_check_failed.summary: A multi-GPU communication check did not pass.
multi_gpu_check_failed.impact: Multi-GPU tensor parallelism may fail to start.

macos_unsupported.label: macOS too old
macos_unsupported.summary: Mac nodes need macOS {{required}} or later; the evidence shows this Mac's version.
macos_unsupported.impact: Environment packages cannot run here, so no instance can be deployed on this node. Upgrade macOS and run the diagnosis again.

macos_idle_sleep.label: Sleeps when idle
macos_idle_sleep.summary: With the settings for its current power source, this Mac goes to sleep after being idle. The agent prevents idle sleep while an instance runs, not otherwise.
macos_idle_sleep.impact: A sleeping Mac is offline: new deployments cannot be scheduled here until it wakes. To keep it available, turn off idle sleep on AC power: sudo pmset -c sleep 0 (the platform does not change this setting).

identity.pending: {{runtime}} is set up on first use
identity.fallback: the agent's own user (uid {{uid}}); the dedicated runtime user is not used because {{reason}}

doctor.injectionExplicit: At deployment gpuworks mounts the accelerator devices into the container itself, only the schedulable cards (OK and warning).
